description: Any http or https address printed as plain text in a terminal is a link. Hover it and it underlines; Cmd-click it on a Mac (Ctrl-click elsewhere, a plain tap on a phone or tablet) and it opens in your system browser. Links a program marks itself keep opening on a plain click. Only http and https ever open. A URL that the program drew across two rows with cursor moves links only its first row.
examples: Claude prints a pull request address: Cmd-click it and the PR opens in your browser.
A dev server prints http://localhost:5173: Cmd-click it to open the app.
On the phone, tap a printed address to open it.
how_to: Move the pointer over an address in a terminal: it underlines.
Hold Cmd (Ctrl on Windows or Linux) and click it. It opens in your system browser.
On a touch screen, tap the address.
media_exempt: a hover underline and a browser opening are not visible in a still capture; recaptured at the version bump
name: Clickable URLs in the terminal
summary: Cmd-click any http or https address printed in a terminal to open it in your system browser.
where: Every terminal: the session page, dashboard cells and viewers.
